statement_record.book: An adjoint square consists of adjunctions <F,G,phi> : X -> A and <F',G',phi'> : X' -> A', functors H : X -> X' and K : A -> A', and natural transformations sigma : F'H -> KF and tau : HG -> G'K such that the hom-set square A(Fx,a) -> A'(F'Hx,Ka) -> X'(Hx,G'Ka) always commutes. Express this condition variously in terms of the units and counits, and prove that each of sigma, tau determines the other. (The case H = K = Id is the conjugate-pair theory of the text.)
statement_record.intree: In an arbitrary bicategory, for internal adjunctions f ⊣ u (from x to y) and f' ⊣ u' (from x' to y') and bounding 1-cells a : x ~~> x', b : y ~~> y', `mate` and `mate_inv` are mutually inverse (mate_roundtrip_left / mate_roundtrip_right) and are packaged as `mate_iso : Isomorphism Sets` between the 2-cell setoids {f' ∘ a ⟹ b ∘ f} and {a ∘ u ⟹ u' ∘ b}. Specialised to Cat (bicat C D ≡ [C,D] definitionally, BicatAdjunction ↔ F ⊣ U), with a := H and b := K these are exactly sigma : F'H ⟹ KF and tau : HG ⟹ G'K, and Cat_mate_unfold_raw gives the unit/counit formula tau_Z ≈ U'(K eps_Z) ∘ U'(sigma_{U Z}) ∘ eta'_{H (U Z)}, restated through the transpose phi' by Cat_mate_unfold.
statement_record.strength_comparison: Mixed. intree-stronger: the correspondence is proved over an ARBITRARY bicategory with arbitrary bounding 1-cells (Mac Lane's exercise is the B = Cat case), it is a full bijection of 2-cell hom-SETOIDS rather than only 'each determines the other', and substituting a = b = Id recovers the section's conjugate pairs. intree-weaker on the condition itself: Mac Lane DEFINES the adjoint square by the commuting hom-set square and asks it be re-expressed via units and counits, whereas in-tree the units/counits pasting IS the definition, the hom-set square is never stated (only its instance at f = ε, which is `Cat_mate_unfold_raw`), and no second equivalent unit/counit form is given. That missing equivalence is already ledgered at maclane:IV.7:def2 and maclane:IV.7:thm2 — the a = b = Id case, both PARTIAL — and since ex4's stated hypothesis IS that hom-set square, this item inherits the gap too: an item cannot be more completely formalized than the special case it generalizes. Its own delta over them, arbitrary bounding functors H and K, is present at full strength.

gap: Mac Lane's adjoint-square CONDITION is never stated in-tree, so what the library proves is a bijection between two 2-cell setoids, not that this bijection is the adjoint-square relation. Precisely: (1) No statement says the hom-set square commutes for ALL f : F x ~> a, i.e. that φ'(K f ∘ σ_x) ≈ τ_a ∘ H (φ f) as functions A(F x, a) → X'(H x, G' K a). At the single instance f = ε_a that square reduces to τ_a ≈ U'(K ε_a) ∘ U'(σ_{G a}) ∘ η'_{H (G a)}, which is verbatim `Cat_mate_unfold_raw` (Instance/Cat/Bicategory/Adjunction.v:244) — so the in-tree content is the value the square forces at one argument, taken as the definition of `mate`, with the 'for all f' half absent. (2) The exercise's first ask — express the condition VARIOUSLY through units and counits — has exactly one in-tree expression, the pasting composite that DEFINES `mate`/`mate_inv` (Mac Lane's (i)/(ii)); the counit and unit forms (his (iii) ε ∘ F τ ≈ ε' ∘ σ G' and (iv) G σ ∘ η ≈ τ F' ∘ η', here bounded by H and K) are nowhere stated; `mate_charac` (Theory/Bicategory/Adjunction.v:347) is only the degenerate f = f', σ = id case. (3) No ordinary-CT restatement over `F ⊣ U` exists: a consumer must transport along `Cat_BicatAdjunction_Adjunction_iff` (Instance/Cat/Bicategory/Adjunction.v:163) and then supply unitor/associator bookkeeping by hand, and there is no corollary specialising `mate_iso` to the shape (F' ◯ H ⟹ K ◯ F) ≅ (H ◯ G ⟹ G' ◯ K). The exercise's second ask — each of σ, τ determines the other — IS present at full strength and in greater generality: `mate_iso` with both round trips, over an arbitrary bicategory and arbitrary bounding 1-cells a, b. This gap is the same one already recorded at maclane:IV.7:def2 and maclane:IV.7:thm2, generalized to arbitrary H, K; Phase E should fold it into that issue rather than file a separate one.
